clips.send: China’s resistance began with Japan’s invasion of northeast China in 1931. Full-scale war began in 1937. In Shanghai, refugees waited to leave. The war ended in 1945. Estimates vary. Historians put Chinese deaths in 1937–1945 at 15–20 million. China’s State Archives reports over 35 million military and civilian casualties over the full period of resistance, including the wounded.

clips.send: In June 1914 two shots on a street in Sarajevo pulled every great power in Europe into war within six weeks. Barely 21 years later an even bigger war began — at the Marco Polo Bridge in China and on the border of Poland — and roughly 70 million people or more died. Why did the alliances fall like dominoes? And why did the Western Front barely move for four years?

clips.send: The Holocaust was Nazi Germany’s planned, state-run genocide: about 6 million Jewish people were murdered, along with millions of others, including Roma, disabled people and political prisoners. Auschwitz-Birkenau, the largest death camp, was liberated by the Soviet Red Army in January 1945.

clips.send: 1914年6月，萨拉热窝街头的两声枪响，六个星期内把欧洲所有大国卷入战争。仅仅21年后，一场更大的战争从中国的卢沟桥和波兰的边境开始，全世界约有7000万人或更多死去。为什么同盟体系像多米诺骨牌一样倒下？为什么西线打了四年却几乎原地不动？
